original_question: For each t >= 5, what is the maximum spectral radius among all F_t-free graphs with m edges, and which extremal graphs attain that value, where F_t = K_1 \/ P_{t-1} is the fan graph on t vertices?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the survey’s fan-graph discussion, whose nearest official formulation is the Yu–Li–Peng fan-graph conjecture reviewed there: for fixed k ≥ 2 and sufficiently large m, obtain a sharp upper bound on λ(G) for graphs with m edges that are F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, together with the equality case.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the forbidden family of fan graphs F_t = K_1 ∨ P_{t-1}, the fixed-edge setting with m edges, and the central edge-spectral Turán objective: maximize the adjacency spectral radius and identify extremal graphs.
missing_details: The nearest official statement is not phrased as an unrestricted exact determination for every t ≥ 5 and every m; it is a sharp upper-bound conjecture for fixed k ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large m.
The paper’s formulation groups the fan graphs as F_{2k+1} and F_{2k+2} for a fixed k, rather than using a single unrestricted parameter t.
The graphs are finite simple undirected graphs, and λ(G) is the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix A(G).
The exact bound is missing: λ(G) ≤ (k − 1 + √(4m − k^2 + 1)) / 2.
The equality case is missing: equality is conjectured to hold exactly for G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m / k) − (k − 1) / 2)K_1.
The qualifier sufficiently large is essential; the threshold depends on the fixed parameter k.
The equality graph only literally exists when (m / k) − (k − 1) / 2 is an integer, so the draft suppresses an implicit divisibility issue in the source formulation.

If one adopts the standard extremal notation used in this literature, the ambient class is often written as the class of F-free graphs with m edges (typically with isolated vertices ignored or excluded); the draft does not specify this surrounding setup.

Because the official formulation is a conjectured inequality plus an equality characterization, rather than a full modulo-by-modulo classification for all m, the draft is slightly broader than the paper-faithful target.
refined_question: Fix an integer k ≥ 2. Is it true that there exists m0 = m0(k) such that, for every m ≥ m0 and every finite simple graph G with m edges that is either F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, where F_s = K_1 ∨ P_{s-1}, one has λ(G) ≤ (k − 1 + √(4m − k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality if and only if G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m / k) − (k − 1) / 2)K_1?
justification: The draft clearly points to the fan-graph line of the survey, but its wording is broader than the paper-faithful target. The nearest official formulation reviewed in this line of work is the paired F_{2k+1}/F_{2k+2} conjecture, not a blanket exact-classification question for all t and all m. The refined version therefore restores the fixed-k parameterization, the sufficiently-large-m quantifier, the exact spectral bound, and the stated equality graph, while avoiding a broader all-moduli extremal-classification claim that the source formulation itself does not make. This is also the formulation later restated as Conjecture 1.1 in the follow-up F6 paper, and the F_{2k+2}-free half is the theorem announced in the Li–Zhao–Zou paper cited in the survey.
